name: client-cart-serviceability-checkout-order-create
executionConcern: owned cart, canonical serviceability, checkout/payment allocation and exactly-once DSH order creation
objective: Close the customer purchase path so owned cart state, address and fulfillment eligibility, checkout/payment references and order creation are canonical, concurrency-safe and fail closed under denial, retry, stale state and dependency failure.
truthOwner: DSH owns cart, serviceability, checkout intent and order operational truth; WLT owns payment allocation and all financial truth.
journeys: exactly-once order creation and immediate readback

tasks.objective: Close owned cart version, idempotency and commercial snapshot truth
tasks.currentProblem: Client cart screens and tests exist, but the current candidate must prove wrong-actor/store isolation, stale-version conflict, replay identity and that prices/items are canonical snapshots rather than local calculations.
tasks.requiredChange: Trace cart reads/mutations from app-client through shared controller/generated contracts to DSH cart handlers/repository/database. Repair object scope, version/idempotency fingerprint and commercial snapshot ownership, then make conflict/success reload committed cart state.
tasks.targetState: Every cart belongs to the authenticated client and intended store, repeated identical mutations replay safely, stale writes conflict, and the client renders server-owned item/price/currency state after each mutation.
tasks.action: Fix DSH cart owner/database constraints first, then shared/app-client consumers and targeted tests.
mustNotChange: Do not trust client-supplied totals/prices as truth.
Do not allow cross-actor or cross-store cart mutation.
Do not overwrite stale versions silently.
Do not use local optimistic state as committed cart truth.
acceptanceCriteria: Wrong actor/store access is denied or hidden.
Identical duplicate mutation returns one effect.
Stale version conflicts and canonical cart reloads.
Commercial item/price/currency state comes from DSH readback.
tasks.rollback: Revert the focused unit commit or roll forward at the canonical owner while preserving durable/audit evidence; never restore local financial or operational truth.
tasks.commitBoundary: One focused cart-owner change plus directly affected client/shared bindings.

tasks.objective: Make one canonical serviceability and fulfillment decision gate checkout
tasks.currentProblem: Address/geofence and operational zone/SLA/capacity/mode rules can diverge if the client or checkout reuses stale/local eligibility; Product Truth requires one DSH decision and explicit fail-closed effects.
tasks.requiredChange: Trace `evaluateDshOperationalPolicy` and address/service-area inputs through shared checkout, DSH platformpolicies/servicearea/checkout and database. Repair inactive-zone, pause, capacity, disabled-mode, version and audit behavior and revalidate before checkout/order command.
tasks.targetState: A client can select only a currently allowed fulfillment mode; inactive, paused, capacity-blocked, mode-disabled or unserviceable states block checkout with actionable canonical readback and cannot be bypassed by stale UI state.
tasks.action: Fix DSH serviceability/policy owner first; change control-panel platform writer only when its versioned mutation/readback causes the same client decision.
mustNotChange: Do not let the client override zone/pause/capacity/mode policy.
Do not use cached discovery eligibility as checkout authorization.
Do not silently fall back when policy dependencies are unavailable.
Do not move policy truth into control-panel UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Every canonical denial blocks checkout/order creation.
Allowed decision includes current version/context needed for safe command validation.
Stale operator policy cannot be bypassed by a previously rendered enabled state.
Policy mutations remain versioned/idempotent/audited at the server owner.
tasks.rollback: Revert the focused unit commit or roll forward at the canonical owner while preserving durable/audit evidence; never restore local financial or operational truth.
tasks.commitBoundary: DSH policy/serviceability correction plus bounded client/control consumer readback only.

tasks.objective: Close checkout intent, WLT payment allocation and exactly-once order creation
tasks.currentProblem: A valid-looking client checkout does not prove that concurrent/repeated submits converge to one order, that immutable snapshots are captured transactionally, or that financial eligibility/allocation remains WLT-owned under timeout and retry.
tasks.requiredChange: Trace checkout intent and order-create commands through generated contracts, DSH checkout/orders/outbox and database, plus WLT-owned payment allocation/reference. Repair idempotency uniqueness, transaction boundaries, immutable snapshots, correlation and unknown financial outcome handling.
tasks.targetState: One eligible checkout intent creates at most one order; repeated/concurrent submit returns the same canonical order, changed payload under the same idempotency identity conflicts, snapshots remain stable, and financial effects/references remain WLT-owned.
tasks.action: Repair DSH/WLT canonical owners and database invariants first; update client success state only after committed order readback.
mustNotChange: Do not create an order before current serviceability/payment eligibility.
Do not create duplicate orders for retry/concurrency.
Do not reprice/rebind an accepted order from live catalog/address after creation.
Do not mutate wallet/ledger/payment truth in DSH/frontend.
acceptanceCriteria: Identical duplicate/concurrent submit creates one order and returns same order identity.
Divergent reuse conflicts without a second effect.
Item/price/currency/address/fulfillment snapshots remain immutable under current contract.
Payment allocation conserves the governed total and DSH stores only allowed references/projections.
Order/outbox effects use one transaction/correlation discipline and retry safely.
tasks.rollback: Revert the focused unit commit or roll forward at the canonical owner while preserving durable/audit evidence; never restore local financial or operational truth.
tasks.commitBoundary: One exactly-once checkout/order owner boundary, with WLT changes only for the same client financial decision.
